questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to combine simple UNIX tools to inspect file content and metadata. It requires robust handling of unreadable files and gzipped content is ignored by design because of -readable and -print0 use. It also demonstrates portability across shells by using POSIX sh constructs only.

## Key Concepts
- find and -readable for safe traversal
- -print0 and while read -d '' to handle spaces
- head to fetch first line, grep -E for pattern matching
- handling missing or nonstandard shebangs with explicit outputs

## Code Example
```bash
find /opt/app/scripts -type f -name "*.sh" -readable -print0 | \
  while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
    first=$(head -n1 "$f" 2>/dev/null)
    if printf "%s" "$first" | grep -E -q '^#!/(bin/(bash|sh)|usr/bin/env (bash|sh))$'; then
      :
    elif printf "%s" "$first" | grep -q '^#!'; then
      echo "$f\tNON_STANDARD_SHEBANG: $first"
    else
      echo "$f\tMISSING_SHEBANG"
    fi
  done
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt this to also consider whitespace before the shebang?
- How would you extend it to also validate that the script is actually executable by its owner?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to reason about cross-format logs, time normalization, and gap detection in a scalable, filesystem-safe way.

## Key Concepts
- Log rotation and mixed formats
- Timestamp normalization to UTC
- Per-host aggregation
- Gap detection across rotated archives

## Code Example
```bash
# Outline (not a full solution)
zcat /logs/**/*.log.gz 2>/dev/null | cat /logs/**/*.log 2>/dev/null | \
awk -v OFS='|' '
  /JSON/ || /{"ts"/ { # parse json ts
        ts=$2; gsub(/[^0-9TZ:-]/, "", ts);
        print "hostX", ts
      }
     /^[0-9]{4}-/ { # parse text timestamps
        if (match($0, /^([0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}) ([0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}):/, m)) {
          print "hostX", m[1" " m[2]
        }
      }
     }' | sort -u | # extract per-host times, then compute gaps
```

- How would you handle divergent timezones across hosts when clock skew is > 1 hour?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical UNIX log processing across mixed formats, compression, and rotations. It also assesses deduplication strategy and time bucketing under real-world constraints.

## Key Concepts
- Mixed log formats (text and JSON)
- Transparent gz handling
- Time bucketing and 45-minute windowing
- Content-hash based deduplication (sha256sum)
- Streaming aggregation (awk/sed) per service

## Code Example
```bash
# Skeleton outline (not a full one-liner)
find /logs -type f \( -name "*.log" -o -name "*.log.gz" \) -print0 | \
  while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
    if [[ "$f" == *.gz ]]; then
      gunzip -c "$f" 2>/dev/null || continue
    else
      cat "$f" 2>/dev/null || continue
    fi
  done | \
  # Process lines, extract timestamps, filter WARN, deduplicate, aggregate
  awk '...process and aggregate...'
```

## Implementation Notes
- Use `find -print0` and `read -d ''` for safe filename handling
- `gunzip -c` for transparent gz decompression
- `2>/dev/null` to skip unreadable files gracefully
- SHA256 hashing for content deduplication across rotations
- Minute-level time bucketing with 45-minute window filter

## Why This Is Asked
Assesses ability to inspect processes and time-based conditions from /proc with POSIX tools, focusing on runtime security and privilege boundaries.

## Key Concepts
- /proc/[pid]/status Uid fields (real vs. effective)
- /proc/[pid]/stat starttime and clock ticks
- /proc/uptime and getconf CLK_TCK for time calculations
- Mapping UID to usernames via getent

## Code Example
```bash
#!/bin/sh
uptime=$(cat /proc/uptime | awk '{print $1}')
clk=$(getconf CLK_TCK)
for p in /proc/[0-9]*; do
  [ -r "$p/status" ] || continue
  ruid=$(awk '/^Uid:/ {print $2}' "$p/status" 2>/dev/null)
  euid=$(awk '/^Uid:/ {print $3}' "$p/status" 2>/dev/null)
  [ -n "$ruid" ] || continue
  st=$(awk '{print $22}' "$p/stat" 2>/dev/null)
  [ -n "$st" ] || continue
  age=$(( (uptime - (st/clk)) ))
  [ "$euid" != "$ruid" ] && [ "$age" -le 300 ] && cmd=$(tr '\0' ' ' < "$p/cmdline" 2>/dev/null)
  user=$(getent passwd "$ruid" | cut -d: -f1)
  printf "%s %s %s %s %s\n" "${p##*/}" "$user" "$cmd" "$euid" "$ruid"
done
```

- What race conditions or permission issues arise, and how would you mitigate them?
